Hi all — following up with the first-pass technical checklist and attachments. See attached: zenith-network-diagram-v1.png and redwood-install-checklist-v0.9.xlsx. Key notes below.

On-prem package (3-node baseline):
- Nodes: 3x GPU hosts (NVIDIA A40 or equivalent) recommended for production throughput.
- Disk: 2TB NVMe local per node (swap/kv-cache + logs); 500GB for /var/lib/redwood by default.
- Memory: 384GB RAM per host recommended for large context sizes.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS preferred; RHEL 8 supported with kernel tweaks (see compatibility matrix).

Networking:
- Private endpoint mode (preferred): outbound HTTPS (443) to Redwood control-plane IP ranges; SSH only for pre-authorized maintenance via bastion; no inbound application ports required.
- VPC peering mode: require route table entries and CIDR non-overlap; require TCP/UDP ports 8443 (control plane), 9090 (metrics) open between peers; optional peering across regions supported but latency-sensitive.
- ACL checklist (excerpts): allow egress to 3 IP ranges (control plane); open ephemeral ports for KV traffic (we list ports in spreadsheet).

Attachments contain: explicit firewall rule examples and a row-level compatibility matrix.

I’ll present the sizing and runbook in the sync if that works.

—Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hey team — quick notes from today’s sync and agreed next steps (captured here for thread):

Summary of decisions:
- Mode: Hybrid — Zenith will start with Private Endpoints for control-plane connectivity; VPC peering planned for later dev/test environments.
- Egress ACLs: Redwood will provide signed IP ranges by Friday 10/16. For now, allow outbound to 52.210.0.0/16, 34.82.0.0/16, and 18.204.0.0/16 (these are example ranges; final list will be signed).
- Air-gapped installs: we support an on-prem bundle but require an initial provisioning step with outbound access to fetch a signed license blob. After provisioning, the system can operate offline. Marcus attached onprem-package-compatibility-matrix.pdf with details.

Action items and owners:
- Redwood (Vivek): produce signed IP ranges + short runbook for Private Endpoint firewall rules (due 2026-10-16).
- Redwood (Marcus): finalize install checklist and disk/GPU sizing doc (due 2026-10-18).
- Zenith (Alex/Priya): confirm CIDR ranges for peering and provide the bastion jump host details (due 2026-10-19).

Open question: Zenith requested RFC-style SLA exceptions for burst capacity during initial integration tests. Vanessa / Laura to scope separately.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
